title: Omoide Yokocho
titleJa: 思い出横丁
summary: A narrow alley of tiny yakitori bars beside the Shinjuku tracks, from the late 1940s. Each bar has 6 to 12 seats. A good first dinner after a long flight.

title: Daikoku Parking Area
titleJa: 大黒PA
summary: A highway rest area inside a giant loop of expressway ramps in Yokohama. It is the most famous JDM car meet in the world. Tuned GT-Rs, Supras, RX-7s and bōsōzoku-style cars park here at night.

title: Hakone Turnpike
titleJa: アネスト岩田ターンパイク箱根
summary: A 14 km private toll road that climbs from Odawara to 1,000 m. Car magazines and TV shows film here because of its long, smooth curves. It was called the Mazda Turnpike before.

title: Taikanzan Viewpoint
titleJa: 大観山
summary: The top of the Turnpike, at 1,011 m. On a clear winter day you see Mt Fuji behind Lake Ashi. The rest area has a café and a car park full of sports cars on weekends.

title: Fun2Drive guided JDM drive
titleJa: Fun2Drive 箱根
summary: This is your sports-car day. Fun2Drive is a small company in Sengokuhara, Hakone. You drive a real JDM car (GT-R, Supra, RX-7, Silvia and others) on the Hakone mountain roads. A guide car leads, so you get the fun roads without getting lost.

title: Otome Pass
titleJa: 乙女峠
summary: The pass from Hakone down to Gotemba. There is a famous view of Mt Fuji from the Otome Pass rest stop. This route avoids the Kagosaka Pass on Route 138, where chains are often required in snow.

title: Oshino Hakkai
titleJa: 忍野八海
summary: Eight clear spring ponds fed by snow melt from Mt Fuji that filters through lava for about 20 years. The village has thatched-roof houses and stalls selling grilled mochi and soba.

title: Chureito Pagoda
titleJa: 新倉山浅間公園 忠霊塔
summary: The five-storey red pagoda with Mt Fuji behind it. This is the most famous photo of Japan. Climb 398 steps up the hill to the viewing deck.

title: Lake Kawaguchi north shore
titleJa: 河口湖 大石公園
summary: The quiet north shore of Lake Kawaguchi. From Oishi Park you see Mt Fuji straight across the lake, often with its reflection on calm winter mornings.

title: Zao Onsen
titleJa: 蔵王温泉
summary: A hot-spring village at 900 m with a ski resort above it. The water is strongly sulfuric and milky, with a smell of eggs. It has been a spa town for about 1,900 years.

title: Zao Onsen Ski Resort
titleJa: 蔵王温泉スキー場
summary: One of the largest ski areas in Japan: 12 courses, 40+ lifts and ropeways, and runs up to 10 km long. Pegasis can ski the long Juhyo course from the top. Aoki learns on the gentle Uenodai slope next to the village.

title: Zao snow monsters
titleJa: 蔵王の樹氷
summary: Fir trees covered in thick rime ice and snow by the winter wind from Siberia. They look like giant white monsters. This happens in only a few places in the world. On some nights they are lit in color.

title: Meito Resort Lucent Takamiya
titleJa: 名湯リゾート ルーセントタカミヤ
summary: Your one onsen ryokan night. It is next to the Zao Ropeway base station. Dinner and breakfast are included, and the sulfur baths are open almost all night. The Takamiya group also lets you use its baths at other inns in the village for free.

title: Sendai Station, Gyutan Street
titleJa: 仙台駅 牛たん通り
summary: Sendai is famous for grilled beef tongue (牛たん, gyūtan): thick slices grilled over charcoal, with barley rice and oxtail soup. Six gyutan shops are in one row on the 3rd floor of the station.

title: Matsushima Bay
titleJa: 松島
summary: One of the Three Views of Japan (日本三景): a bay with about 260 small islands covered in pine trees. Walk across the red Fukuura bridge and see Godaido temple on its small island. Try the grilled oysters in winter.

title: Kanemori Red Brick Warehouses
titleJa: 金森赤レンガ倉庫
summary: Harbour warehouses from 1887, now shops, a beer hall and cafés. In January the harbour is lit with a Christmas-style tree and lights, and the snow on the bricks looks great at dusk.

title: Mount Hakodate night view
titleJa: 函館山
summary: One of the three great night views of Japan. From the top at 334 m you see the city lights on a narrow neck of land between two dark bays.

title: Hakodate Morning Market
titleJa: 函館朝市
summary: About 250 stalls selling crab, sea urchin (uni), salmon roe (ikura) and squid. At the squid-fishing pool (活いか釣堀) you catch a live squid and they slice it for you on the spot.

title: Goryokaku Fort
titleJa: 五稜郭
summary: A star-shaped fort from 1864, the last battlefield of the samurai civil war. Go up Goryokaku Tower to see the full star shape covered in snow.

title: Onuma Quasi-National Park
titleJa: 大沼公園
summary: A frozen lake with small islands and the volcano Komagatake behind it. In winter you can try ice fishing for smelt (wakasagi) in a tent on the ice, and they fry your catch as tempura.

title: Niseko Grand Hirafu
titleJa: ニセコ東急 グラン・ヒラフ
summary: World-famous for light, dry powder snow ("Japow"), with Mt Yotei, the "Fuji of Hokkaido", across the valley. Late January is the peak of the powder season.

title: Otaru Canal
titleJa: 小樽運河
summary: A canal lined with stone warehouses and gas lamps. With snow on everything it looks like an old postcard. It was the setting of the film Love Letter (1995), very popular in China.

title: Sakaimachi Street
titleJa: 堺町通り
summary: A street of old merchant houses now full of glass shops (Kitaichi Glass), music boxes, and dessert shops like LeTAO. The music box museum at the end has a steam clock.

title: Otaru Sushi Street
titleJa: 寿司屋通り
summary: A street with about 20 sushi shops. Otaru is a fishing port, and winter fish is at its best.

title: Asahikawa Ramen Village
titleJa: あさひかわラーメン村
summary: Eight famous Asahikawa ramen shops under one roof. Asahikawa style is a soy-sauce soup made with pork and seafood, with a thin layer of lard on top to keep it hot in the cold.

title: Asahiyama Zoo penguin walk
titleJa: 旭山動物園
summary: In winter, a group of king penguins walks a 500 m loop through the snow between the visitors. The zoo is also famous for its tunnel under the penguin pool and its polar bears.

title: Shirogane Blue Pond, winter light-up
titleJa: 白金青い池
summary: A pond whose water is blue because of minerals from the volcano above. In winter it is frozen and covered in snow, and dead trees stand in it. At night it is lit with changing colors.

title: Shirahige Falls
titleJa: 白ひげの滝
summary: Water pours out of the rock face into a bright blue river, framed by snow and ice. See it from the bridge in Shirogane Onsen. It is lit at night.

title: Shibuya Sky
titleJa: SHIBUYA SKY（渋谷スカイ）
summary: An open-air roof deck 230 m above the Shibuya Scramble crossing. On a clear winter evening you see Mt Fuji at sunset, then the whole of Tokyo lights up.

title: Sapporo Beer Museum
titleJa: サッポロビール博物館
summary: A red-brick brewery building from 1890. The beer garden next door serves all-you-can-eat Jingisukan (grilled lamb) with beer.

title: Jingisukan Daruma
titleJa: 成吉思汗だるま 本店
summary: The most famous Jingisukan restaurant in Sapporo, since 1954. You grill lamb and onions on a dome-shaped iron pan at a small counter. Chinese and Japanese guides both rank it number one.

title: Nijo Market
titleJa: 二条市場
summary: A central market for crab, uni and salmon roe rice bowls. Good for a seafood breakfast.

title: Soup Curry GARAKU
titleJa: スープカレー GARAKU
summary: Soup curry is a Sapporo invention: a thin, spicy curry soup with big pieces of chicken and grilled vegetables. GARAKU is one of the most popular shops.

title: Odori Park and Sapporo TV Tower
titleJa: 大通公園・さっぽろテレビ塔
summary: The long park in the city centre. In early February the Snow Festival builds giant snow sculptures here. You leave 3 days too early, but you may see the sculptures being built.

title: Mt Moiwa night view
titleJa: もいわ山
summary: A ropeway to a viewpoint with the whole of Sapporo lit up below. It is on Japan’s "new three great night views" list.

title: Naritasan Shinshoji Temple
titleJa: 成田山新勝寺
summary: A large temple founded in 940, with a three-storey pagoda and a big park. The street up to it, Omotesando, is famous for grilled eel (unagi) shops.

title: Tamagawa Miharashi Park
titleJa: 多摩川見晴らし公園
summary: The wide concrete steps on the bank of the Tama River. In episode 2, Momoka plays guitar here at night and talks with Nina. It is also on the key art. Across the river you see Tokyo.

title: Minamikawara Park and Miyakocho Footbridge
titleJa: 南河原公園・都町歩道橋
summary: The neighbourhood near Nina’s apartment. The footbridge over the main road is in the opening animation, and the small park appears in many scenes. Japanese guides call it a must-see.

title: MUZA Kawasaki Symphony Hall
titleJa: ミューザ川崎シンフォニーホール
summary: On the 2F walkway Nina trips and Momoka’s guitar falls in episode 1. The public upright piano on 1F is in the music video. Animate Kawasaki (anime goods) is on 2F.

title: Lazona Kawasaki Plaza, Rufa Square
titleJa: ラゾーナ川崎プラザ ルーファ広場
summary: The open-air stage inside the big shopping mall west of the station. Nina, Momoka and Subaru play "声なき魚" here in episode 3. You get the anime angle from the 4F and 5F walkways. HMV on 4F sells collaboration goods.

title: Kawasaki Station East Exit Plaza
titleJa: 川崎駅東口 駅前広場
summary: The most important Girls Band Cry spot. In episode 1 Nina hears Momoka playing on the street here, and the reunion and final scenes come back to this plaza. Street musicians still play here in the evening.

title: Marufuku Coffee, Kawasaki Azalea
titleJa: 丸福珈琲店 川崎アゼリア店
summary: The retro coffee shop where the band meets. It is on B1F of the Azalea underground mall, below the East Exit plaza. It has stamp number 1 of the stamp tour, and the official GBC stamp gallery is also in Azalea.

title: CLUB CITTA' and La Cittadella
titleJa: クラブチッタ（ラ チッタデッラ）
summary: The live house where the band plays its final show in episode 13, inside an Italian-style shopping street. The real band TOGENASHI TOGEARI has played here. Tower Records and Village Vanguard nearby sell GBC goods.

title: Suga Shrine stairs
titleJa: 須賀神社（男坂）
summary: The red-railed stairs where Taki and Mitsuha pass each other and turn around at the end of the film. It is the image on the poster, and one of the most photographed anime spots in Tokyo.

title: Shimokitazawa
titleJa: 下北沢
summary: The home of Kessoku Band. A neighbourhood of small live houses, used-clothing shops and record stores. The Senrogai open space (Ep 5) is on the old railway line above the station.

title: Shimokitazawa SHELTER
titleJa: 下北沢SHELTER
summary: The basement live house that is the model for STARRY, where Bocchi’s band plays and works. Fans photograph the stairs going down from the street.

title: Nakano Broadway
titleJa: 中野ブロードウェイ
summary: A 1960s shopping building. Floors 2 to 4 are full of shops for used figures, manga, trading cards and old toys, including many Mandarake shops. Less crowded and often cheaper than Akihabara.

title: Akihabara ZEST
titleJa: 秋葉原ZEST
summary: A small live venue in Akihabara. It is the model for "BEAST", where Ai performs and baby Aqua and Ruby dance with glow sticks in episode 1. The front of the building matches the anime.

title: Akihabara Radio Kaikan
titleJa: 秋葉原ラジオ会館
summary: The most famous building in Akihabara: 10 floors of figures, trading cards, model kits and anime goods, opposite the station. In Steins;Gate a satellite crashes into its roof.

title: Kinshi Park
titleJa: 錦糸公園
summary: The park in Sumida where Chisato and Takina talk in episode 1. There is a Lycoris Recoil manhole cover in front of the Olinas mall next to it, and Tokyo Skytree stands just behind.

title: Sabbat of the Witch Kansai ending
titleJa: サノバウィッチ 聖地巡礼（京都・大阪・神戸）
cost: Flight Hokkaido→Osaka approx 12,000–25,000 JPY; local trains approx 3,000 JPY; hotels as normal
duration: 3 days (replaces Furano→Sapporo, Sapporo day, and changes end city to Osaka)
summary: Sabbat of the Witch (Yuzusoft, an Osaka company) uses real places in Kyoto, Osaka and Kobe, not the Tokyo area. Fly Sapporo/Asahikawa to Osaka on day 13, see Kyoto (station, the school model at Kyoto Concert Hall, Sanjo shopping street), Osaka Grand Front and the Kobe Kitano Starbucks cafe, then fly home from Kansai.
hook: Walk into Sabbat of the Witch's real Kyoto, Osaka and Kobe backgrounds.
why: It is the only way to see the Sabbat places; Kansai also has Uji (Euphonium) and Toyosato (K-On) close by, and Kansai Airport has many flights to Shanghai.
winterNote: All city spots, no snow problems. Kyoto Concert Hall is a working concert hall: outside photos only. Kobe Starbucks was renovated, so the inside differs from the game CG. Pegasis's Narita flight would

title: Aokana pilgrimage, Goto Islands
titleJa: 蒼の彼方のフォーリズム 聖地巡礼（五島列島）
cost: New Chitose→Fukuoka approx 15,000–30,000 JPY; Fukuoka↔Goto Fukue (ANA/ORC) approx 15,000–25,000 JPY each way; rental car approx 6,000 JPY/day (all approx, not checked)
duration: 3 days (2 nights Fukuoka/Goto); 4 days to add Naru Island and Hisaka Island by ferry
summary: Verified: the Four Islands of Aokana are modelled on the Goto Islands, Nagasaki (Fukue, Hisaka, Wakamatsu, Nakadori, Naru). Fly Hokkaido→Fukuoka, then a 40-min flight to Goto Fukue; rent a car for Takahama Beach (Flying Circus practice), Osezaki Lighthouse (date scene), Fukue samurai street (Misaki's house) and the Fukue arcade, then fly home from Fukuoka.
hook: Fly to the real Four Islands where Aokana's kids race in the sky.
why: The main anime wish that no other part of the trip covers; the island coast is also very beautiful and quiet in winter.
winterNote: No snow, but strong winter wind can cancel jetfoils and small planes; keep a spare half day. No direct Tokyo flight: go via Fukuoka (40 min, ANA/ORC) or Nagasaki (30 min), or jetfoil Nagasaki→Fukue 1

title: Sabbat plus Aokana west ending
titleJa: 関西・五島 聖地巡礼ルート
cost: Flight Sapporo→Osaka approx 12,000–25,000 JPY; Shinkansen Shin-Kobe→Hakata approx 15,000 JPY; Fukuoka↔Goto approx 15,000–25,000 JPY each way (approx)
summary: One route that does both big wishes: shorten Hokkaido, fly Sapporo→Osaka, one day Kyoto/Uji, one day Osaka/Kobe, Shinkansen Shin-Kobe→Hakata (about 2 h 15), fly to Goto Fukue, then home from Fukuoka. This drops Asahikawa, Biei and Furano.
hook: Three dream anime places in one trip: Kyoto, Uji and Goto.
why: Covers Sabbat of the Witch and Aokana inside Aoki's 15-day limit.
winterNote: Goto flights/jetfoils can stop in strong wind; put Goto before the last day, not on it. Loses the Asahiyama zoo and Blue Pond days.

title: Kaguya-sama walk, Mita to Takeshiba
titleJa: かぐや様は告らせたい 聖地巡礼（三田・田町・新橋・竹芝）
cost: approx 500 JPY trains
summary: Kaguya-sama is set in Minato ward, Tokyo: the school walk is Mita-dori by Keio University, the shared-umbrella scene is Mita Kokusai Building, and the fireworks-night meeting point is Takeshiba Pier. Walk Tamachi → Mita → Shimbashi SL Plaza → Takeshiba (2–3 h), ideally at dusk for the bay view.
hook: Walk Kaguya and Shirogane's school route, then end at the fireworks pier.
why: Easy Tokyo add-on on the JR Yamanote line, no extra travel day.
winterNote: City streets, open all year. The actual fireworks in the story are in Kisarazu (Chiba) in summer; in winter you only see the pier. Shinomiya house model (Tsunamachi Mitsui Club) is private: outside on

title: Girls Band Cry: Yako and stamps
titleJa: ガールズバンドクライ 矢向・幸区・スタンプツアー
cost: Sento approx 550 JPY; stamp book approx 1,000–2,000 JPY (not checked); trains approx 500 JPY
summary: Extra GBC places not in the plan: Yako Station and the Yako-yu bathhouse (Nina's area, ep 1–2), Saiwai green path, and Shinmei Shrine by Kawaracho estate (ep 12 'ROCK no Kamisama', ep 13). Collect the official 'Girls Band Cry Stamp Tour' stamps (stamp book sold at stamp spots) and, if time, FRO CAFE at Musashi-Kosugi.
hook: Go deep into Nina's Kawasaki neighbourhood and collect Girls Band Cry stamps.
why: Deepens the Kawasaki day with the quiet local spots fans love, and you can take a real sento bath where Nina did.
winterNote: Yako-yu opens 15:00–22:00, irregular closing days. FRO CAFE 11:30–21:00, closed Mondays. Stamp tour has grown to 25+ spots (e.g. Kawasaki Aquarium and Kawasaki Daishi from Feb 27, 2026); check the lis

title: Girls Band Cry Tokyo scenes
titleJa: ガールズバンドクライ 東京編（東京駅・渋谷・武道館）
cost: approx 500 JPY trains
summary: GBC also uses Tokyo: the Tokyo Station Marunouchi South dome (ep 1, Nina arrives), Shibuya Hachiko and Spain-zaka (ep 3), Cafe Renoir by Shibuya Hands (ep 4) and the Nippon Budokan (ep 6). Easy to fit between other Tokyo stops.
hook: Stand where Nina first steps into Tokyo in Girls Band Cry.
why: Fans of the show can add these with almost no extra travel time.
winterNote: Public places, open all year. Budokan is outside only unless there is a concert.

title: More Bocchi spots in Shimokitazawa
titleJa: ぼっち・ざ・ろっく！ 下北沢 聖地（本多劇場・どんぐりひろば公園ほか）
cost: free
summary: Beyond the station and SHELTER: Honda Theater ('Honmaru Gekijo' in the show), Donguri Hiroba park with spring-ride toys (ep 4), the Senrogai empty lot with the big pipe (ep 5), the 'Geki' small theater wall (ep 1) and the 'artist photo' ivy wall at Times Shimokitazawa 8. About half of the 50+ Bocchi spots are here.
hook: Find the small corners of Shimokitazawa where Bocchi hides and hopes.
why: Turns a quick stop into a full Bocchi walk in the same area on day 2.
winterNote: The Times parking ivy wall is in a road-widening zone and may be gone; winter ivy has no leaves. Photos of SHELTER only on weekdays, small groups. Do not photograph private houses.

title: Bocchi's home town, Kanazawa-hakkei
titleJa: ぼっち・ざ・ろっく！ 金沢八景（横浜市）
cost: approx 800 JPY trains
summary: Bocchi lives in the Kanazawa-hakkei area of Yokohama. See Kanazawa-hakkei Station and the Seaside Line overpass benches where Hitori and Kikuri play on the street (ep 6), Biwajima Shrine and the Hiragata Bay promenade.
hook: Visit Bocchi's home town, where she plays her first street live.
why: Quiet, few tourists, and on the same Keikyu line as Kawasaki (about 30 min), so it fits the Kawasaki day.
winterNote: Outdoor seaside spots, open all year; short winter daylight, go in the morning.

title: Enoshima and Slam Dunk crossing
titleJa: 江の島・鎌倉高校前踏切
cost: approx 2,000 JPY trains
summary: Ride the Enoden to the Kamakura-Koko-mae rail crossing from the Slam Dunk opening, then walk to Enoshima for Bocchi episode 9 (Katase-Enoshima station, Asahi tako-senbei, Enoshima Shrine red torii). Clear winter days often show Mt Fuji across the bay at sunset.
hook: See the Slam Dunk crossing, then climb Enoshima like the Bocchi band.
why: Two famous anime spots plus sea and Fuji views in one easy day from Tokyo.
winterNote: Open all year; winter has clearer air for Fuji. The crossing is very busy and has guards; stay on the sidewalk and do not stand in the road.

title: Numazu, Love Live! Sunshine!!
titleJa: ラブライブ！サンシャイン!! 沼津・内浦
cost: approx 5,000–8,000 JPY (bus/train + Shinkansen Mishima→Tokyo)
duration: 1 day (replaces the afternoon in Tokyo / Shibuya Sky)
summary: On the way back from Fuji, go to Numazu instead of straight to Tokyo: Uchiura bay with Yasudaya Ryokan (Chika's house model), Awashima island and Izu-Mito Sea Paradise, then Numazu town with Aqours manholes and shops. Return by Shinkansen from Mishima.
hook: Walk Aqours' seaside home town, with Mt Fuji over Uchiura bay.
why: One of the biggest pilgrimage towns in Japan (Anime Tourism 88), and the sea with Fuji behind it fits the Fuji days.
winterNote: Mild coast, no snow. Awashima island cafe/boat has its own opening days; check before going.

title: Yuru Camp Motosu lake view
titleJa: ゆるキャン△ 浩庵キャンプ場（本栖湖）
cost: free (parking small fee may apply)
summary: Koan Campsite on Lake Motosu is where Rin camps in Yuru Camp episode 1 and Nadeshiko sees Fuji; it is also the Fuji view on the 1,000-yen note. About 25 min by car west of Kawaguchiko.
hook: Stand where Rin camps and Nadeshiko sees Fuji in Yuru Camp episode 1.
why: Yuru Camp is a winter-camping anime, so late January is the exact season of the show, and you already have a car on day 4.
winterNote: Very cold at dawn; roads can be icy, winter tyres needed. Best Fuji view in the morning.

title: Hakodate: Saint Snow and Conan
titleJa: 函館 聖地巡礼（ラブライブ！サンシャイン!!・名探偵コナン）
cost: approx 1,500–3,000 JPY (ropeway, tram, Goryokaku Tower)
summary: Hakodate is an Anime Tourism 88 spot for Love Live! Sunshine!! S2 ep 8–9 (Saint Snow's family cafe model Sabo Kikuizumi, Kanemori red brick warehouses, Mt Hakodate night view). The 2024 Conan movie 'The Million-dollar Pentagram' uses Goryokaku, and Golden Kamuy uses the Benten Daiba fort site.
hook: Walk snowy Hakodate, home of Saint Snow and Conan's star fort.
why: Already on the route; the snowy night view is also how the Aqours episode looks.
winterNote: Snowy slopes in Motomachi; wear shoes with grip. Mt Hakodate ropeway runs in winter but can stop in strong wind.

title: Otaru anime and Golden Kamuy
titleJa: 小樽 聖地巡礼（ゴールデンカムイ・最終兵器彼女）
cost: free
summary: Otaru appears in Golden Kamuy (Taisho Glass main shop), Saikano (Otaru Canal, Asahi lookout, aquarium) and Hidamari Sketch x Honeycomb (canal, former NYK building, music box museum). A short walk while you pass Otaru.
hook: See Otaru's snowy canal and glass shops from Golden Kamuy and Saikano.
why: Small bonus on a day already in Otaru; the snowy canal is a classic winter photo.
winterNote: Otaru Snow Light Path festival is usually in early/mid February, so likely after your visit; check 2027 dates.

title: Ghibli Museum, Mitaka
titleJa: 三鷹の森ジブリ美術館
cost: 1,000 JPY adult
summary: Studio Ghibli's own museum with a short film only shown there. Timed tickets only, sold online; 15 min by train from Shinjuku plus a walk along the Tamagawa aqueduct.
hook: Enter Miyazaki's own museum and see a short film shown nowhere else.
why: Must-see for anime fans, and it is close to the Shinjuku hotel.
winterNote: Tickets for January go on sale Dec 10, 2026, 10:00 JST (Lawson Ticket, overseas site) and sell out fast. Usually closed Tuesdays (Jan 19, Jan 26, Feb 2) and in some maintenance periods; check the Jan

title: Chichibu: Anohana and icicles
titleJa: 秩父 聖地巡礼（あの花・ここさけ・空の青さを知る人よ）
cost: approx 3,000–4,000 JPY trains
summary: Chichibu is the town of Anohana, Kokosake and Her Blue Sky (all Anime Tourism 88). See the old Chichibu Bridge from the Anohana ending, Chichibu Shrine and the station area, 80 min from Ikebukuro by Seibu Laview.
hook: Cross the bridge from the Anohana ending, then see blue winter icicles.
why: The classic tear-jerker pilgrimage, and in winter the Misotsuchi icicles nearby are a big bonus.
winterNote: Misotsuchi icicles (三十槌の氷柱) usually show mid-Jan to late Feb with some evening light-ups; check 2027 dates. Cold, but little snow in town.

title: Washinomiya Shrine, Lucky Star
titleJa: らき☆すた 鷲宮神社
cost: approx 1,500 JPY trains
summary: The shrine of the Hiiragi sisters in Lucky Star, the place that started modern anime pilgrimage in Japan. Buy an ita-ema, see the fan boards; about 1 h from Tokyo by Tobu line.
hook: Visit the shrine from the Lucky Star opening, where anime pilgrimage began.
why: Historic spot for anime fans, short trip.
winterNote: New Year crowds are over by late January; open all year.

title: Oarai, Girls und Panzer
titleJa: ガールズ&パンツァー 大洗
cost: approx 5,000–8,000 JPY trains
summary: Oarai town is covered with Girls und Panzer panels and shop tie-ins; see the Kamiiso torii on the rocks at Oarai Isosaki Shrine and the Marine Tower area. About 2 h from Tokyo via Mito.
hook: Visit the seaside town where tanks crash through real shops in Girls und Panzer.
why: One of the friendliest anime towns in Japan (Anime Tourism 88), plus winter monkfish (anko) hot pot.
winterNote: Winter is anko season. Windy on the coast. Kamiiso torii sunrise is a famous photo.

title: Hida: Your Name and Hyouka
titleJa: 飛騨古川・高山（君の名は。・氷菓）
cost: approx 15,000–20,000 JPY trains (Tokyo→Toyama Shinkansen + Takayama line) plus ryokan
summary: Hida-Furukawa Station and Keta Wakamiya Shrine are Your Name scenes; Takayama old town and Nakabashi bridge are Hyouka's Kamiyama city. Deep snow in January makes it a winter postcard.
hook: Walk the snowy towns of Your Name and Hyouka.
why: Two big titles in one snowy old town, a different winter scene from Zao.
winterNote: Snow and cold; Takayama line can delay in heavy snow. No ski resort for Pegasis unless you add one. Returning north to Hokkaido needs a long day via Tokyo.

title: Uji Euphonium and Toyosato K-On
titleJa: 宇治（響け！ユーフォニアム）・豊郷小学校旧校舎群（けいおん！）
cost: approx 1,000–3,000 JPY trains
summary: Only with a Kansai ending: Uji Bridge and Daikichiyama lookout from Hibike! Euphonium (30 min from Kyoto), and the old Toyosato school, the K-On school model with the tea-time club room (1 h from Kyoto).
hook: Run Kumiko's bridge in Uji, then drink tea in the K-On club room.
why: Adds two much-loved Kyoto Animation settings to the Sabbat Kansai days.
winterNote: Daikichiyama is a short hill hike, can be icy. Toyosato old school is open to visitors on most days; check closed days.

title: Hakone as Evangelion Tokyo-3
titleJa: 箱根（エヴァンゲリオン 第3新東京市）
cost: free
summary: Evangelion's Tokyo-3 is set in Hakone (Sengokuhara and Lake Ashi area). Look for Eva tie-ins around Hakone-Yumoto and Owakudani on the drive day.
hook: Drive through Hakone, the real ground under Evangelion's Tokyo-3.
why: Small anime bonus on a day already in Hakone.
winterNote: Eva shops and collab items change often; not checked for 2027. Owakudani can close due to volcanic gas.

title: Rusutsu snow drift driving course
titleJa: ルスツリゾート 雪上ドリフト
cost: Ride-along Subaru B4 ¥17,000 (1–2 people), GT-R or GR Yaris ride ¥27,000; drive yourself: intro 30 min ¥31,000, full course 75 min ¥61,000; rear-seat rider ¥10,000–20,000
summary: A closed snow course at Rusutsu Resort, about 40 min from Niseko, with Subaru, GT-R and GR Yaris cars. You can ride with a pro rally driver (4 min) or drive yourself with an instructor next to you (30 or 75 min).
hook: Slide a 4WD Subaru sideways across a snowed-in golf course.
why: The only real 'you drive, you drift' option on the route that does not need a 3-year licence: Pegasis can drive on private ground, and Aoki can ride along or drive too.
winterNote: Season mid-Dec 2026 to late Feb 2027. Slots 8:30, 10:00, 13:00, 15:00. Book by 17:00 the day before. Driving needs a valid licence (bring IDP); instructor can refuse you if unsafe. No minimum years st

title: Initial D Mt Haruna day trip
titleJa: 頭文字D 聖地 榛名山（秋名山）
cost: Rental car ~¥10,000–15,000/day shared + fuel/tolls; museum fee: check
duration: 1 day (about 2–2.5 h each way from Tokyo by car)
summary: Drive from Tokyo to Gunma and run the real 'Akina' downhill (Prefectural Route 33) past the Yaseone old toll gate and the five hairpins to Lake Haruna. Stop at Ikaho Onsen stone steps and the Ikaho toy and car museum, which shows a Fujiwara Tofu Shop display.
hook: Drive Takumi's real tofu run down 'Akina' to Lake Haruna.
why: It is the number one JDM pilgrimage site, and it mixes the anime and car interests with an onsen town.
winterNote: Road is open in winter, but it is at high altitude with snow and ice risk Dec–Mar. Studless tyres are a must; both can drive a normal rental car; Aoki takes the icy parts. Go only on a clear day. Add

title: Irohazaka hairpins and Nikko
titleJa: いろは坂（日光）
cost: approx ¥6,000–9,000 return train (Tobu line) + local bus; check current fares
summary: Irohazaka is two one-way mountain roads with 48 hairpins (20 up, 28 down) to Lake Chuzenji. You can ride it on the normal local bus from Nikko station, then see Toshogu shrine and the Akechidaira view.
hook: Ride a normal city bus up 48 hairpins, each one marked with a letter.
why: It is the home road of team Emperor in Initial D Third Stage, and nobody needs to drive, so Pegasis's licence does not matter.
winterNote: Road is open all year (free road since 1984), but snow and ice are common in late Jan; buses still run. Some upper sights may be closed in winter. Self-drive only with studless tyres (Aoki).

title: Frozen lake ice driving, Nagano
titleJa: 女神湖 氷上ドライブ
cost: Per car per day ¥30,000–53,000 (lunch included), passenger +¥2,500
summary: Lake Megami (1,540 m) freezes in winter and becomes an ice course where cars slide from 20 km/h. Clubs and driving coaches run full-day ice lessons with lunch.
hook: Learn to steer with the throttle on a frozen lake 1,540 m up.
why: Ice car control on private ground is the dream JDM winter skill, and Pegasis can drive there.
winterNote: 2026 dates were e.g. Jan 19–20, Jan 31–Feb 2, Feb 6–7; 2027 dates not yet out. Most events need YOUR OWN car (studless, under 2.5 t), so it is hard for tourists. Fun2Drive (Hakone rental) ran a rental

title: Ebisu Circuit drift taxi (closed)
titleJa: エビスサーキット ドリフトタクシー
cost: ¥45,000 per car (max 3 people) + ¥500 insurance each
summary: Famous drift passenger ride in Fukushima, near the Tohoku Shinkansen route. A pro drifts you around the circuit with up to 3 riders per car.
hook: A D1 champion drifts you around Ebisu in a Mark II taxi.
why: Would be the perfect Tohoku stop, but it does not run in the trip dates.
winterNote: Closed in winter: Dec 20 – Mar 31 (snow). Official page also showed 'temporarily closed' in 2026. Do not plan it for Jan 2027.

title: Guided circuit drift day from Tokyo
titleJa: ドリフト体験ツアー（東京発）
cost: ¥75,000–205,000 depending on car; ¥100,000 refundable deposit
summary: Tour companies pick you up in central Tokyo and take you to a circuit to drive or ride in a real drift car, with instructor and lunch. About 6 h of track time.
hook: Pick your JDM hero car, from R34 to Nismo GT-R, and drift it.
why: A full drift day for JDM fans; Aoki can drive and Pegasis can ride if too young or too new to drive.
winterNote: Driver must be 26+ with IDP; passengers any age. Which circuit is used in winter is not stated (Ebisu is closed in winter) — ask the operator before booking.

title: Fuji Motorsports Museum and Speedway
titleJa: 富士モータースポーツミュージアム
cost: Adult ¥1,800 weekday at the window (¥1,600 online)
summary: Museum at the gate of Fuji Speedway with about 100 years of race cars from Toyota, Nissan, Honda and others. You can also look at the circuit and Mt Fuji behind it.
hook: See the Le Mans-winning Mazda 787B next to Fuji Speedway.
why: It sits between Hakone and Kawaguchiko on day 4, so it is an easy stop for race-car fans.
winterNote: Open daily 10:00–17:00, no regular closed day. Online booking opens the month before and gets priority.

title: Nissan Heritage Collection, Zama
titleJa: 日産ヘリテージコレクション（座間）
cost: Free (reservation required)
summary: A garage in Nissan's Zama plant holding about 400 historic cars: Skyline GT-Rs, race cars, Z cars. Timed guided visits of about 80 minutes; on weekdays they sometimes start engines.
hook: Walk rows of 300 Nissans, and hear some of them start.
why: The best GT-R and Skyline collection in the world, free, one hour from Shinjuku.
winterNote: Weekdays only (Mon–Fri, about 10:00–16:00); Jan 19–22 are weekdays. Apply online in Japanese and wait for approval; slots fill fast, so apply about 1 month ahead.

title: Tatsumi PA and Umihotaru night
titleJa: 辰巳第一PA・海ほたるPA
cost: Free entry; expressway tolls (Aqualine to Umihotaru) or a guided night tour (price varies by company)
summary: Add Tatsumi PA (small car meet spot with a city skyline view) and Umihotaru (rest stop island in Tokyo Bay) to the Daikoku PA night. You reach them only by car on the expressway.
hook: Sit in a JDM meet under the city lights, then drive under the sea.
why: More night car-meet spots on the same drive as Daikoku, with Aoki at the wheel or with a guided JDM night tour.
winterNote: Meets are best on Friday/Saturday nights; Jan 21, 2027 is a Thursday, so fewer cars. Police sometimes close PAs at night when crowded.

title: Nissan Crossing Ginza showroom
titleJa: NISSAN CROSSING（ニッサン クロッシング）
cost: Free (café extra)
summary: Nissan's free showroom at the main Ginza crossing, with new and special cars and a café. Easy 30-minute stop in central Tokyo.
hook: Free Nissan showroom on the most famous corner in Ginza.
why: Quick free car stop in the city on the anime day.
winterNote: Open all year; check the site for cars on display in Jan 2027.

title: Honda Collection Hall, Motegi
titleJa: ホンダコレクションホール（モビリティリゾートもてぎ）
cost: No extra museum fee; pay resort entrance + parking only (check fee)
duration: half day + 2.5 h travel each way
summary: Honda's own museum inside the Motegi circuit, with F1 cars, NSX, Type R and motorbikes. Entry is included in the resort ticket.
hook: Honda keeps about 350 machines here, and all of them still run.
why: Honda heritage in one hall; can pair with Nikko/Irohazaka as a north Kanto car day.
winterNote: Check the Motegi opening calendar for late Jan 2027. Hard without a car (bus from Utsunomiya is limited).

title: Start trip at Tokyo Auto Salon
titleJa: 東京オートサロン2027
cost: Ticket ¥3,000 Sat/Sun (09:00–19:00 / 18:00), ¥4,000 Fri (public from 14:00); digital advance tickets only
duration: 1 day at show; whole trip shifts ~4 days earlier
summary: The biggest tuning car show in Asia, at Makuhari Messe near Narita, Jan 15–17, 2027. Arrive Jan 14–15, spend Saturday at the show, then run the same route 4–5 days earlier.
hook: Asia's biggest tuning show fills eleven halls near Narita.
why: Every JDM tuner, demo car and drift star in one place — the peak event for their interests.
winterNote: Aoki's 15-day visa limit means an earlier end: about Jan 15 – Jan 29. Flights are not booked yet, so this is possible. Weekend is very crowded; go at opening.

title: Up Garage used parts, Sapporo
titleJa: アップガレージ 札幌
cost: Free to browse
summary: Up Garage is a big chain of used car parts shops: wheels, steering wheels, shift knobs, JDM small parts. Several stores are in Sapporo.
hook: Dig through used JDM parts bins for cheap car souvenirs.
why: Good place for cheap JDM souvenirs (shift knobs, badges) on the last Sapporo day.
winterNote: Stores are in the suburbs; go by car or taxi. Check each store's hours.

title: Toyota Automobile Museum, Nagoya
titleJa: トヨタ博物館
cost: Adult fee: check official site (about ¥1,200 in past years)
summary: Large museum of about 140 cars from all makers in the world, plus Japanese car history. It is in Nagakute, east of Nagoya.
hook: About 150 cars from all makers, with the Toyota 2000GT as the star.
why: Only worth it if the route changes to go via Nagoya (for example flying out of Nagoya).
winterNote: Open 9:30–17:00, closed Mondays. Far from the current route.

title: Shirakawa-go light-up, then fly north
titleJa: 白川郷ライトアップ・飛騨高山・金沢
cost: Light-up bus from Takayama 13,000–16,000 (incl. entry); Tokyo→Takayama ~15,000; flight Komatsu→Sapporo ~20,000–35,000

hook: Thatched farmhouses glowing in deep snow, one of four nights a year.
why: Snow-covered thatched farmhouses lit at night are one of the most famous winter views in Japan, and the Jan 24 date falls exactly on baseline day 6.
winterNote: 2027 light-up days: Jan 11, 17, 24, 31, 17:30–19:30. Full advance reservation, no tickets on the day. Nouhi bus tours from Takayama go on sale online Oct 13–Nov 2, 2026 (staggered); inn-with-deck-tick

title: Snow monkeys and Shiga Kogen ski
titleJa: 地獄谷野猿公苑・志賀高原・渋温泉

summary: Take the Hokuriku Shinkansen to Nagano, walk 35–40 min through snow to see wild monkeys in a hot spring, and stay in Shibu or Yudanaka onsen town. Ski Shiga Kogen (or Nozawa Onsen) the next day, then go back via Omiya and take the Hayabusa to Shin-Hakodate on day 8.
hook: Wild monkeys soaking in a steaming hot spring while snow falls on them.
why: It replaces Zao with a ski-plus-onsen stop that also has the famous snow monkeys, and Shiga Kogen has easy runs for Aoki and big terrain for Pegasis.

title: Japan Alps: Matsumoto, Hakuba, Kanazawa
titleJa: 松本城・白馬・金沢
cost: Matsumoto Castle 1,300 (1,200 e-ticket); Hakuba lift ~8,000–10,000 (not verified for 2026–27); Komatsu→Sapporo flight ~20,000–35,000

hook: A black samurai castle in snow, then ski an Olympic downhill run.
why: Hakuba is a world-class ski area for Pegasis, Matsumoto is one of Japan's original castles, and it removes the long Tohoku rail days.

title: Gala Yuzawa Shinkansen ski day
titleJa: GALA湯沢スキー場
cost: Lift 1-day 7,300 (2025–26); Shinkansen ~7,000 each way; JR 'SKISKI' packs can be cheaper
summary: Take the Joetsu Shinkansen from Tokyo straight to Gala Yuzawa station, which opens directly into the ski resort gondola. Ski all day with rental gear, soak in the onsen at the base, and be back in Tokyo in the evening.
hook: Step off the bullet train and walk straight into the ski rental shop.
why: It is the easiest real ski day from Tokyo (about 75–90 min), with beginner slopes for Aoki, and it can replace the long trip to Zao.
winterNote: 2025–26 season ran Dec 20–May 6; 2026–27 dates not yet published. Gala Yuzawa station runs only in ski season. Weekends are crowded; Jan 24–25 is Sun–Mon.

title: Fujiten ski with Fuji view
titleJa: ふじてんスノーリゾート
cost: Lift 1-day 5,500 weekday / 6,500 weekend (2025–26); rental extra
summary: Small ski resort on the north side of Mt Fuji, about 20 min by car from Lake Kawaguchi. Aoki can take a beginner lesson while Pegasis skis, with Mt Fuji right above the slopes.
hook: Learn to ski with Mt Fuji filling the sky above the slope.
why: It adds skiing to the Fuji days and gives Aoki an easy first day before the bigger resorts in Hokkaido.
winterNote: 2025–26 season: Dec 13–Apr 1, lifts 9:00–16:30, night ski on weekends/holidays until 21:00. Jan 23 (day 5) is a Saturday, so night ski is possible. Snow is mostly machine-made.

title: Diamond Fuji sunset at Yamanaka
titleJa: 山中湖 ダイヤモンド富士
cost: free
summary: At Lake Yamanaka the sun sets exactly on the top of Mt Fuji from mid Oct to late Feb, and the place moves around the lake each day. In late Jan it is seen from the north shore (Oike beach, Nagaike) at about 15:55–16:15.
hook: The setting sun sits exactly on Fuji's peak like a diamond ring.
why: A short, free photo stop that fits the Fuji day after the Hakone drive, and it is one of the best-known winter Fuji views.
winterNote: Official list: Oike beach until ~Jan 30 (~16:03), Yanagashiri until ~Jan 27 (~15:55), Nagaike lakeside until ~Feb 5 (~16:13). Needs clear sky; check the exact spot for Jan 22/23 on the Yamanakako site

title: Lake Motosu and lava ice caves
titleJa: 本栖湖・鳴沢氷穴・富岳風穴
cost: Each cave ~350–500 (check); free lake
summary: Walk into Narusawa Ice Cave and Fugaku Wind Cave, lava tubes in the Aokigahara forest where ice stays all year. Then drive to Lake Motosu, the view of Mt Fuji printed on the 1,000-yen note.
hook: Crawl into a frozen lava tube, then see the view on Japan's money.
why: Aoki can drive the quiet lake roads west of Kawaguchiko, and it is a different Fuji view from Chureito with few people.
winterNote: Cave temperature 0–3°C all year. Winter opening hours were not confirmed; check the official site. Lake roads can be icy early in the morning.

title: Fuji-Q rides and ice skating
titleJa: 富士急ハイランド
cost: Rink or free-pass tickets: check official site (not verified)
summary: Theme park at the foot of Mt Fuji with extreme roller coasters and a 400 m outdoor skating rink (SEIKO-OVAL) in winter. Ride coasters with Mt Fuji in view, then skate with rental skates.
hook: Skate a 400 m outdoor ice oval under Mt Fuji.
why: It is next to Kawaguchiko station, so it fits the Fuji days with no extra travel.
winterNote: Outdoor rink open early Dec to late Feb. Some coasters stop in strong wind or snow.

title: Owakudani and Open-Air Museum
titleJa: 大涌谷・箱根彫刻の森美術館
cost: Ropeway ~1,500–2,500 one way; museum ~2,000 (check)
summary: Ride the Hakone Ropeway over the steaming volcanic valley of Owakudani and eat the black eggs cooked in the hot springs. Stop at the Hakone Open-Air Museum, a large sculpture park with a foot bath.
hook: Fly over a steaming volcano crater and eat eggs boiled black in it.
why: It fits between the Hakone Turnpike drive and Kawaguchiko, with Mt Fuji views from the ropeway on clear winter days.
winterNote: Ropeway Dec–Jan 9:00–16:15; it stops in wind of 30 m/s or more and has yearly maintenance closures, so check the operation page.

title: Gotemba outlets with Fuji view
titleJa: 御殿場プレミアム・アウトレット
cost: free entry
summary: Large outlet mall on the east side of Mt Fuji, on the road from Hakone to Kawaguchiko. Shop for ski wear and brand goods with Fuji in the background.
hook: Buy cheap ski wear with Mt Fuji right behind the shops.
why: It is directly on the day 4 driving route and is a cheap place to buy winter gear before the ski days.
winterNote: Open all winter; the Fuji view is best on clear mornings.

title: Atami plum garden and Izu drive
titleJa: 熱海梅園・伊豆スカイライン
cost: Plum festival entry ~300 (check); car rental and tolls extra
summary: Aoki drives from Hakone down to Atami, a seaside onsen town, and sees early plum blossoms at Atami Baien. The Izu Skyline toll road along the mountain ridge is an extra option with sea and Fuji views.
hook: Japan's earliest plum blossoms, then a ridge road above the sea.
why: A car-focused day with onsen and early flowers, close to the Hakone Turnpike.
winterNote: 2026 plum festival ran Jan 10–Mar 8; 2027 dates not yet published, likely similar. Kawazu cherry festival 2027 is Feb 6–Mar 7, so it is AFTER this trip. Ridge roads can be icy in the morning.

title: Kusatsu Onsen night in snow
titleJa: 草津温泉
cost: Bus ~3,500–4,500 each way (check); yumomi show 700; ryokan 15,000–25,000
summary: Direct highway bus from Tokyo (Yaesu 7:10, arrives 11:35) to Kusatsu, one of Japan's top onsen towns. See the steaming Yubatake hot-water field lit at night, watch the yumomi water-cooling show, and ski at Kusatsu Onsen ski area.
hook: A town-square river of steaming hot water, lit up at night in snow.
why: Strong onsen town with snow and light skiing, and a simpler, closer alternative to Zao.
winterNote: Yumomi show 6 times a day at Netsu-no-yu. Paths around Yubatake freeze, wear good shoes. From Kusatsu, going north to Hokkaido means back through Tokyo/Omiya.

title: Gokayama Ainokura quiet window lights
titleJa: 五箇山 相倉合掌造り集落
cost: free village entry; parking fee
summary: Smaller, quieter thatched-roof village than Shirakawa-go, in deep snow. On Wed Jan 27, 2027 there is a 'window light' evening (17:00–20:00) where you see the village at night with house lights only.
hook: A snowed-in thatched village lit only by the windows of people living there.
why: A calm backup if Shirakawa-go light-up tickets are sold out, and it fits a Hokuriku route.
winterNote: Main 2027 winter light-up is Feb 20–21 (after the trip). Window-light days: Jan 13 and Jan 27, 2027. Jan 27 only fits if the Hokuriku plan is shifted by 1 day.

why: Mixes two anime settings, a famous snow village, real Alps skiing for Pegasis and easy slopes for Aoki, and onsen monkeys.

title: Kyushu: Goto islands and onsen drive
titleJa: 九州：五島列島・阿蘇・別府
cost: transport approx. ¥60,000–85,000 pp (Haneda→Fukuoka ~¥12,000–30,000, Fukuoka⇄Fukue ~¥11,000 each way on ANA/ORC, rental car 6 days + fuel + tolls split by 2 ~¥30,000). Flight change: return from Fukuoka (FUK) — direct to Shanghai; Pegasis connects via Tokyo or Seoul. No skiing, no Hokkaido.
summary: D6 fly Haneda→Fukuoka, Hakata yatai stalls · D7 fly to Goto Fukue, rent car, Aokana spots (samurai street, Takahama Beach, Osezaki Lighthouse) · D8 Goto, fly back · D9 car to Kumamoto Castle · D10 Aso crater area + Milk Road → Kurokawa Onsen · D11 Yamanami Highway → Yufuin · D12 Beppu hells + sand bath · D13 back to Fukuoka · D14 fly home from Fukuoka.
hook: Fly to the real Aokana island, then drive volcano roads between Japan's best onsen.
why: Warmer roads let Aoki drive a lot, it has a rare anime island, and some of Japan's best onsen towns.
winterNote: Kyushu is mild (5–10 °C) but Aso and the Yamanami Highway can freeze or close after snow; ask the rental shop for snow tyres. Goto flights can cancel in strong winter wind.

title: Hokkaido deep: drift ice and powder
titleJa: 北海道周遊：流氷とパウダースノー

hook: Break sea ice on a ship, float in it, then watch cranes dance in snow.
why: Pure snow country: drift ice, cranes, Hokkaido powder for Pegasis and wide easy runs for Aoki, with long snowy drives for Aoki.
winterNote: Aurora icebreaker runs Jan 20–Mar 31 2027, but drift ice usually reaches Abashiri only around late January and is best in February; if no ice, the cruise still runs. Eastern Hokkaido roads are icy; lo

title: Tokyo base with day trips
titleJa: 東京拠点の日帰り旅
cost: transport approx. ¥40,000–55,000 pp (GALA Yuzawa Shinkansen round trip ~¥14,000 x1–2, Nikko ~¥6,000, Kusatsu bus ~¥5,000 each way, Hakone Free Pass ~¥6,100, Kamakura ~¥2,000). Flight change: round trip to Tokyo only (simplest, cheapest flights).
summary: D6 Shinkansen to GALA Yuzawa ski (station is at the ski base) · D7 Nikko Toshogu + Kegon Falls · D8 bus to Kusatsu Onsen, stay in a ryokan · D9 Kusatsu ski → Tokyo · D10 Kamakura + Enoshima (Slam Dunk crossing) · D11 Hakone onsen + ropeway · D12 GALA ski again or Kawagoe · D13 Tokyo shopping · D14 Tokyo, fly out. One hotel for most nights.
hook: One Tokyo hotel, but still ski, onsen, and Fuji views most days.
why: Least packing and moving, still gives ski days, onsen and Fuji views, and keeps Tokyo nights for anime and car meets.
winterNote: GALA Yuzawa usually opens mid-December to early May. Nikko roads above Kegon can be icy; trains and buses run.

titleJa: 伊豆・富士・信州・群馬 ドライブ旅

title: Hokkaido snow to Okinawa sun

hook: Leave minus 10 °C snow and land in 20 °C sun and pink cherry blossoms.
why: A warm 17–20 °C ending after two weeks of snow, with an easy coast drive for Aoki and Japan's earliest sakura.

hook: Five short hops west, each with Fuji, a hot bath or cars.
why: It turns the Tokyo–Osaka move into five small trips with Fuji, onsen, cars and Ghibli, and no day has more than 1 h 30 min on trains.
winterNote: New route days 5–9. Weekday traps: Hobby Square, Suzuki museum and Toyota Commemorative Museum close on Mondays; Ghibli Park and SCMaglev park close on Tuesdays (Jan 26 closed); Toyota Kaikan closes S

title: Two-day Tokaido: Shizuoka, Hamamatsu, Nagoya
titleJa: 東海道 2日間（静岡・浜松・名古屋）
cost: Trains ≈ ¥13,400 pp (Tokyo→Shizuoka ¥6,270 + Shizuoka→Hamamatsu ¥2,330 + Hamamatsu→Nagoya ¥4,840) + buses/ropeway ≈ ¥2,700 + museums ¥1,000–1,200
summary: A fast version of the westward move that uses the weekend. D7 continue

why: Pegasis and Aoki see Fuji country, two car museums and a Shinkansen simulator but lose only one day against a direct train.
winterNote: New route days 5–6. Suzuki Museum: free, booking needed; on weekdays Sep–Jan visitors enter only after 15:00 (school groups), so the Sunday slot matters. Nihondaira ropeway has a planned stop Dec 1–21

title: Hakone as first stop, no suitcases
titleJa: 箱根を西行きの最初の宿に（手ぶら観光）
cost: Freepass (Hakone area, from Odawara) 2 days ¥6,000 + Odakyu Shinjuku–Odawara ¥910 + Romancecar ¥1,200; luggage ¥1,500 per bag each way; ryokan extra
summary: Make Hakone the first night of the westward trip instead of a day trip from Tokyo. Take the Romancecar to Hakone-Yumoto, hand bags to the station luggage counter, loop Hakone with the Freepass, then leave west by Tokai Bus from Moto-Hakone to Mishima (via Mishima Skywalk) or by Tozan train to Odawara and the Shinkansen.
hook: Arrive in Hakone with empty hands, leave west over Mishima Skywalk.
why: It saves the trip back to Tokyo and gives one ryokan onsen night before the business hotels start.

title: Atami early cherry blossoms at night
titleJa: あたみ桜 糸川桜まつり・熱海温泉泊
cost: Tokyo→Atami Hikari ¥4,070 reserved; Atami→Shizuoka Kodama ¥3,100; festival free; onsen hotel extra
summary: Stop one night in Atami, the seaside onsen town 36 min from Tokyo by Hikari. The Itokawa river walk has 'Atami-zakura', Japan's earliest cherry blossoms, lit up every night during the January festival; then soak in a hotel onsen above the bay.
hook: Pink cherry blossoms in January, lit over a small river by the sea.
why: Real cherry blossoms in January, plus an onsen night by the sea, on the direct line west.
winterNote: New route day 5. 2026 festival: Jan 10–Feb 8, light-up daily 16:30–23:00, weekend free sakura tea; 2027 not announced, likely similar. Kawazu cherry festival is later (2026: Feb 7–Mar 8). No Atami fir

title: Shuzenji onsen night in Izu
titleJa: 修善寺温泉
cost: Mishima→Shuzenji ¥550 each way (Atami→Shuzenji direct Odoriko ¥1,840); ryokan with 2 meals often ¥15,000–30,000 pp (check)
summary: A quiet, old onsen town in the middle of Izu, 37 min from Mishima by the local Sunzu Line. Walk the bamboo forest path and the river with Tokko-no-yu, stay in a ryokan, and come back to Mishima for the Shinkansen west.
hook: A river, a bamboo path and a ryokan in the middle of Izu.
why: A more traditional onsen night than Hakone, easy to add between Hakone/Mishima and Shizuoka.
winterNote: New route days 5–6. Mild, no snow. Tokko-no-yu is now for viewing only (no bathing). Kawazu cherry blossoms (further south) start in February, after this trip.

title: Numazu port seafood and deep-sea aquarium
titleJa: 沼津港・沼津港深海水族館
cost: Aquarium adult ¥2,200; seafood bowl about ¥1,500–3,000 (check); Mishima→Numazu local ¥200s
summary: Stop at Numazu port on the way west: eat a fresh aji (horse mackerel) or seafood bowl at the port restaurants, then see the Deep Sea Aquarium with frozen coelacanths. Until Jan 31, 2027 it has a 'Godzilla Minus Zero' collab with Godzilla figures and design material.
hook: Frozen coelacanths and Godzilla, next to Japan's deepest bay.
why: Seafood lunch plus a Godzilla show fits a Hakone → Mishima → Shizuoka day, and adds to the Love Live stop if they want it.
winterNote: New route day 6. Godzilla −0.0 collab: Oct 3, 2026 – Jan 31, 2027 (stickers for the first 25,000 visitors from Dec 1). Aquarium 10:00–18:00 (hours change by season). The existing Numazu Love Live idea

title: Nihondaira Fuji view and Kunozan ropeway
titleJa: 日本平・日本平ロープウェイ・久能山東照宮
cost: Bus Shizuoka Sta→Nihondaira ¥710 one way; ropeway round trip ¥1,250; shrine admission extra (check); Hobby Square free
summary: From Shizuoka Station take the bus to the Nihondaira hilltop for a wide Fuji and Suruga Bay view, then ride the 5-min ropeway down to Kunozan Toshogu, the first shrine of Tokugawa Ieyasu. Back in town, the free Shizuoka Hobby Square (Tamiya, Bandai, Hasegawa) is 1 min from the station.
hook: Fuji over the bay, then a cable car down to a golden shrine.
why: The best Fuji view on the Tokaido line, a national treasure shrine, and Shizuoka's model-kit culture for anime and car fans.
winterNote: New route days 6–7. Winter air gives the clearest Fuji. Ropeway daily, Nihondaira dep. 9:10–16:45; planned stop Dec 1–21, 2026 only. Hobby Square 11:00–18:00 weekdays, 10:00–18:00 weekends, closed Mon

title: Lake Hamana ropeway, oysters and unagi
titleJa: 浜名湖・かんざんじロープウェイ・舘山寺温泉
cost: Bus Hamamatsu Sta→Kanzanji about 45 min (fare check); ropeway round trip ¥1,300 (¥1,700 with music-box museum); unagi meal about ¥4,000–6,000 (check)
summary: Stay a night at Kanzanji Onsen on Lake Hamana, 45 min by bus from Hamamatsu Station. Ride Japan's only ropeway that crosses a lake, then eat winter lake food: unagi, Hamamatsu gyoza and the local 'kaki kaba-don' (grilled oyster bowl).
hook: A ropeway over the lake, eel for lunch, oysters for dinner.
why: Eel, oysters and a salty onsen by a lake: a food night between Shizuoka and Nagoya with Fuji on clear days.
winterNote: New route day 7. Ropeway 10:00–17:30 in normal season; check the operating calendar. Oyster kaba-don and wild tora-fugu are winter dishes here. Pal Pal amusement park has its own winter days.

title: SCMaglev and Railway Park, Nagoya
titleJa: リニア・鉄道館
cost: Adult ¥1,200; N700 simulator ¥500 (first come, limited); Aonami Line Nagoya→Kinjo-futo ¥360, 24 min
summary: JR Central's train museum by Nagoya port: 39 real trains, from steam engines to Shinkansen and the maglev test car, plus Japan's largest railway diorama. Try the N700 Shinkansen driving simulator.
hook: Drive a Shinkansen, then stand beside the maglev test car.
why: After riding the Shinkansen west, they can drive one in the simulator and see the record-breaking maglev.
winterNote: New route day 9 (or any day but Tuesday). 10:00–17:30, last entry 17:00, closed Tuesdays (Jan 19, 26, Feb 2). Simulator tickets sell out; on busy days they hand out numbered tickets before opening.

title: Ghibli Park in winter
titleJa: ジブリパーク

hook: Walk into Totoro's house and Kiki's town in the same day.
why: The biggest anime place on the Tokaido route, and it fits the Nagoya stop.

title: Nagoya food, Osu and the castle
titleJa: 名古屋めし・大須商店街・名古屋城

summary: One Nagoya day for its own food: hitsumabushi (eel on rice, eaten 3 ways) at Atsuta Horaiken near Atsuta Shrine, miso katsu at Yabaton's main shop in Osu, and spicy tebasaki wings at night. Walk Osu Kannon and the Osu shopping streets, and see Nagoya Castle's rebuilt Honmaru Palace.
hook: Eel three ways, a pork cutlet in red miso, and wings at midnight.
why: Three famous local dishes in one day, plus Osu's anime, figure and used-goods shops.

title: Nozawa ski, then Hokuriku west
titleJa: 野沢温泉スキー・白川郷・金沢・永平寺→京都

summary: D5 (Sat Jan 23) Hakutaka Tokyo→Iiyama (1 h 51, ¥8,360 unreserved), Nozawa Onsen Liner bus (25 min, ¥600), ski the afternoon, soak in the free wooden soto-yu baths · D6 (Sun Jan 24) ski until 11:00, Iiyama→Kanazawa (1 h 18, ¥6,730), 14:30 Hokutetsu light-up tour to Shirakawa-go with deck ticket (back 21:50, ¥18,500) · D7 (Mon) Kenrokuen early free entry, Omicho crab, Higashi Chaya (museum closed Mo

titleJa: 国宝松本城氷彫フェスティバル・プロジェクションマッピング

why: The same snow-roof farmhouse scene, 10 minutes from Takayama, for ¥300 and without a lottery.

title: Shinhotaka Ropeway and Okuhida onsen
titleJa: 新穂高ロープウェイ・奥飛騨温泉郷（平湯・福地）
cost: 'Okuhida Marugoto Value Kippu' 2-day from Takayama ¥7,700 (bus Takayama–Shinhotaka + ropeway round trip; ropeway alone ¥3,800); Hirayu no Mori day bath ¥700

cost: Google Flights Jan 28, 2027 (seen Sep 2026): Jetstar 9:50 7,110 JPY; Peach 12:35/16:15/17:45 7,850 JPY, 7:20/10:00/13:55 9,050 JPY. Checked bag: Jetstar 15 kg 2,030-2,500 JPY at booking (2,990+ later), skis +2,500; Peach about 2,000 JPY web / 3,100 airport (2025). Rapi:t 1,670 JPY
summary: The cheapest way north: Peach (8 flights a day, 7:20-17:45) or Jetstar (9:50) from Kansai Airport to New Chitose, 1 h 55 min, from 7,110 JPY on Jan 28, 2027. Take the Rapi:t from Namba (about 38 min, 1,670 JPY) and add a checked bag when you book.
hook: Blue Rapi:t train to the sea airport, two hours later you land in snow.
why: It is under half the price of JAL/ANA, has flights all day, and KIX is 40 minutes from Namba where the Osaka days end.
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11. Schedules for Jan 2027 are open. Snow at New Chitose can delay or cancel flights; LCCs rebook only on their own (few) flights, so take a morning flight. Peach uses KIX Terminal

title: Fly Itami to Sapporo (JAL/ANA)
titleJa: 伊丹空港→新千歳空港（JAL・ANA）
cost: JAL 13,030 JPY (7:35, 11:45, 15:00, 18:20), 16,330 JPY (10:50, 12:45); ANA price not shown on Google Flights, usually similar: check ana.co.jp. Limousine bus 730 JPY
summary: Itami is the city airport, 25-35 minutes by limousine bus from Osaka station or Namba (730 JPY). JAL (7:35, 11:45, 15:00, 18:20, from 13,030 JPY on Jan 28, 2027) and ANA (about 7 flights, 8:30-19:05) fly to New Chitose in 1 h 45-50 min, with a 20 kg bag free.
hook: The easy airport: bus from Umeda, big-airline seat, bag free.
why: Less travel time than KIX, a free bag, and more flights to rebook onto if Hokkaido snow cancels one.
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11. Jan 2027 schedules open. Snow delays at New Chitose are common, but JAL/ANA have many flights to change to. For East Hokkaido: JAL via CTS to Memanbetsu (7:35 or 11:45 start) 1

title: Fly Kobe to Sapporo on Skymark
titleJa: 神戸空港→新千歳空港（スカイマーク・AIRDO）
cost: Skymark 17:25 9,070 JPY, 15:05 11,470 JPY, 8:05/9:00 12,570 JPY; AIRDO 10:30 9,965 JPY (Jan 28, 2027). Umeda to Kobe Airport by train about 700 JPY, about 1 h
duration: about 4 h door to door from Osaka
summary: Kobe Airport, on an island 18 minutes from Sannomiya by Port Liner (340 JPY), has Skymark (8:05, 9:00, 15:05, 17:25), AIRDO (10:30, 19:00) and ANA (8:40) to New Chitose, 1 h 50 min, from 9,070 JPY. Skymark and AIRDO include a 20 kg bag.
hook: A small island airport, a free suitcase, and near-LCC prices.
why: Nearly LCC prices with a free checked bag, and it fits well if you spend the last Kansai night in Kobe (beef, harbor lights) instead of Osaka.
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11. Schedules open. Kobe Airport is small and fast: check-in 20 min before is often enough, but Skymark has fewer flights to rebook onto after a snow cancellation.

title: Fly Itami straight to Asahikawa
titleJa: 伊丹空港→旭川空港（JAL）
cost: 18,960 JPY (JAL, Jan 28, 2027); rental car one-way Asahikawa to New Chitose adds a drop fee
duration: flight 1 h 45 min; changes the Hokkaido order
summary: One JAL nonstop a day, 8:45 to 10:30 (1 h 45 min, 18,960 JPY on Jan 28, 2027), lands you next to Biei and Furano. Start Hokkaido with the Blue Pond, Asahiyama Zoo and Furano skiing, then drive west to Sapporo and fly home from New Chitose.
hook: Breakfast in Osaka, the Blue Pond in snow before lunch.
why: It skips the 2-hour drive from Sapporo to the snow country and gives a clean one-way route through Hokkaido, ending near the international airport.
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11. Only one nonstop (8:45), so leave Osaka hotel by about 7:00. Asahikawa Airport handles snow well but can still close in storms. There is no nonstop from Kansai Airport (Jetstar

title: Fly Itami to Hakodate
titleJa: 伊丹空港→函館空港（JAL・ANA）
cost: JAL 11:10 17,930 JPY; ANA 8:20 and 15:30 price not shown on Google Flights (check ana.co.jp)
summary: Three nonstops a day: ANA 8:20, JAL 11:10 (17,930 JPY on Jan 28, 2027) and ANA 15:30, about 1 h 30 min. Start Hokkaido in Hakodate (night view, morning market, Love Live Saint Snow places), then drive Onuma, Niseko, Otaru, Sapporo like the old baseline.
hook: From Osaka to Hakodate's famous night view in one afternoon.
why: It keeps the good south-to-north Hokkaido road trip of the first plan without the long Shinkansen from Tokyo.
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11. Schedules open. No flights from Kansai Airport to Hakodate. Hakodate is milder than inland Hokkaido; roads to Niseko are snowy.

title: Overnight ferry Maizuru to Otaru
titleJa: 新日本海フェリー 舞鶴→小樽
cost: Tourist A bed 12,000 JPY (fare period A, Oct 2026-Jan 2027); private rooms more; bus Osaka-Maizuru about 2,300 JPY
duration: 1 night + 1 full day (21 h at sea)
summary: Instead of flying, take a bus from Umeda to Maizuru (about 2 h, about 2,300 JPY) and board the Shin Nihonkai ferry at 23:50; it sails up the Sea of Japan for 21 hours and arrives in Otaru at 20:45 the next evening. Beds from 12,000 JPY (Tourist A), with a big bath on board.
hook: Sleep on the Sea of Japan and wake up sailing toward Hokkaido.
why: A slow, different travel day with sea baths and snow on the Hokkaido coast, arriving in Otaru, which is already on the route.
winterNote: New route day 10 departure, day 11 arrival 20:45: it uses a full day. Daily 'with exceptions': check the monthly ship schedule (配船表) for Jan 2027 dock days. Winter sea can be rough; take seasickness p

title: Tokaido anime and car road west
titleJa: 東海道 聖地巡礼＆クルマ旅（富士→浜松→名古屋→鈴鹿→京都）

hook: Six days west: anime towns in the morning, race cars and car factories in the afternoon.
why: It is one line of travel with no going back, and every day has both an anime place and a car place, which is what both of them like most.
winterNote: New route day 5–10. The order matters: Suzuka Circuit is CLOSED Jan 12–21 and Jan 26–29, 2027 (open Jan 22–25), so Suzuka must be D5–D7. Toyota Commemorative Museum is closed Mondays (Jan 25), Toyota

title: Yuru Camp west: Minobu, Fujinomiya
titleJa: ゆるキャン△ 身延・富士宮 聖地巡礼
cost: Rental car approx 8,000–12,000 JPY/day, or JR Minobu line approx 1,500 JPY; manju approx 80 JPY each; yakisoba approx 700 JPY
duration: 1 day (by car, or JR Minobu line)
summary: Leave Kawaguchiko to the west instead of going back to Tokyo: past Lake Motosu to Kai-Tokiwa Station and the old Shimobe school (model of Motosu High School), then Minobu Station street and Minobu manju. Go south to Fujinomiya: Fujisan Hongu Sengen Taisha and Fujinomiya yakisoba (S2 ep 7), then the Tokaido line at Fuji.
hook: The quiet valley town where the Outdoor Activities Club goes to school.
why: It turns the Fuji days into the start of the trip west, with the home town of Nadeshiko and Rin that the covered Motosu campsite stop does not show.
winterNote: New route day 5 (Kawaguchiko → Tokaido). The school model (旧下部小・中学校) can be seen only from outside. It opens inside only at events (e.g. Nov 28, 2026); no January 2027 event is announced. Route 300 pa

title: Yuru Camp S2: Rin's New Year trip
titleJa: ゆるキャン△ SEASON2 浜名湖・御前崎 聖地巡礼
cost: Local trains approx 1,000 JPY; Hamamatsu gyoza approx 1,000 JPY; eel bowl approx 4,000–6,000 JPY
duration: half day (Bentenjima, Kanzanji) to 1 day (with Omaezaki, by car)
summary: In Yuru Camp Season 2 ep 1–3, Rin rides west over New Year: Omaezaki Lighthouse, Kakezuka Lighthouse, Mitsuke Tenjin in Iwata, the Nagisaen campsite and the red torii at Bentenjima on Lake Hamana, Kanzanji Onsen and the Okuhamanako lookout. Stop in Hamamatsu for a half or full day on the way to Nagoya.
hook: Follow Rin's New Year scooter trip, in the same cold January light.
why: The story happens in late December and January, so the winter light and cold wind match what they will see.
winterNote: New route day 5 or 6. Mild coast, no snow; strong dry west wind in January. Bentenjima torii is best at sunset (about 17:15 in late Jan). Omaezaki is far from the train: needs a car.

title: Hamamatsu: Suzuki, Yamaha, Honda roots
titleJa: 浜松・磐田 ものづくりの街（スズキ歴史館・ヤマハ発動機コミュニケーションプラザ）
cost: Free entry at both museums; local trains approx 500 JPY
summary: Hamamatsu is where Suzuki, Yamaha and Honda started. See the free Suzuki History Museum (looms from 1909, old cars and bikes, how cars are made today; book ahead) and Yamaha Motor's free Communication Plaza in Iwata (racing bikes, engines; renewed June 2026). With a car, add the Honda Soichiro Monozukuri museum in Tenryu.
hook: One city gave the world Suzuki, Yamaha and Honda. Both museums are free.
why: It is JDM history for free and fits on the Tokaido line between Fuji and Nagoya.
winterNote: New route day 6 (Sun Jan 24) is best. Suzuki History Museum: reservation only, closed Mondays; Sep–Jan weekdays are for school trips, so normal visitors only from 15:00 on weekdays. Bookings open abou

title: Suzuka Circuit: drive the F1 track
titleJa: 鈴鹿サーキット サーキットチャレンジャー
cost: Entry 2,000–2,400 JPY adult (web is 500 JPY less), EV kart 2,000 JPY per kart (up to 3 people)
summary: Suzuka Circuit, home of the Japanese F1 GP, has a park where anyone can drive an EV kart on the real racing course (East Course) with no licence needed. Walk the grandstand and the pit side, and see the Honda race cars on show.
hook: No licence needed: you drive the real Suzuka F1 East Course yourself.
why: Pegasis cannot rent a car with 1 year of licence, but here both of them can drive on an F1 track.
winterNote: New route day 5–7 ONLY. Official: closed Jan 12–21 and Jan 26–29, 2027 for checks, so it is open Jan 22–25 (Fri–Mon). Winter hours about 10:00–16:30. Circuit Challenger tickets are online only (Asovie

title: Toyota day: Commemorative Museum, Kaikan
titleJa: トヨタ産業技術記念館・トヨタ会館
cost: Commemorative Museum 1,000 JPY; Toyota Kaikan free; trains approx 1,500 JPY
summary: Start at the Toyota Commemorative Museum by Nagoya Station, in Toyota's first red-brick loom factory: looms, then cars built step by step with robot demos. Then go to Toyota City for the free Toyota Kaikan Museum by the head office, with new Toyota, Lexus and GAZOO Racing cars and a new 'how Toyota builds cars' area (June 2026).
hook: From wooden looms to GR race cars, in Toyota's own home town.
why: It adds the factory side of Toyota to the covered Toyota Automobile Museum, and both are easy by train.
winterNote: New route day 8 (Tue Jan 26) fits: the Commemorative Museum is closed Mondays (Jan 25), Toyota Kaikan is closed Sundays. Real plant tours at Toyota City stay stopped (notice 2023, still up in 2026); o

title: Nagoya: Medalist rink and Osu
titleJa: メダリスト 聖地巡礼 大須（名古屋スポーツセンター）
cost: Skating 1,500 JPY + skate rental 500 JPY; Osu street food approx 1,500 JPY
summary: The figure skating anime Medalist (S2 aired Jan 2026) is set in Nagoya. Skate at the real home rink of Inori's club, Osu Skating Rink, see Osu Kannon and the Fuji-shaped slide at Uramonzen park (taiyaki scene, ep 3), and walk Osu shopping street, also used in Yatogame-chan. Near Nagoya Station, Coffee House Kako is Rin's breakfast cafe in the Yuru Camp movie.
hook: Skate on the real rink where Inori trains in Medalist.
why: Skating in winter where the anime was drawn is fun for both, and Osu is Nagoya's otaku and food street.
winterNote: New route day 6–8. Osu rink public hours: weekdays 12:00–18:00, weekends 10:00–18:00; closed only Jan 1 (it can be booked out for events; check the site). Wear gloves on the ice.

title: Chihayafuru: Omi Jingu, Otsu
titleJa: ちはやふる 聖地 近江神宮
cost: Shrine free; clock museum small fee; train from Kyoto approx 200–400 JPY
summary: Omi Jingu in Otsu is the 'holy place' of competitive karuta and the key place of Chihayafuru: the Meijin and Queen title matches are held every January in its Omi Kangakudo hall. Walk the vermilion gate and shrine, and see the clock museum with about 2,300 clocks.
hook: The shrine where Chihaya dreams of becoming Queen of karuta.
why: It is 10 minutes from Kyoto by train and is one of the big anime places in Kansai that the old plan did not have.
winterNote: New route day 9. The 2026 Meijin/Queen matches were on Jan 10–11, before this trip; 2027 dates not yet announced but likely early January too. Omi Kangakudo is a working hall: outside only when there

title: Demachi: Tamako Market, Eccentric Family
titleJa: 出町桝形商店街・下鴨神社（たまこまーけっと／有頂天家族）
cost: Free; mame-mochi at Demachi Futaba approx 250 JPY
summary: Demachi Masugata shopping street in Kyoto is the model for Usagiyama street in KyoAni's Tamako Market: find the mackerel object, the Tamako pictures and the fan notebook. Cross the Kamo river delta to Shimogamo Shrine and Tadasu no Mori, where the tanuki family lives in The Eccentric Family.
hook: Tamako's mochi street and the tanuki forest, one river apart.
why: Two well-loved Kyoto anime in a 1-hour walk, with mochi and a winter forest.
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10. City spots, open all year. Some shops in the arcade close on Tuesdays or at irregular days; Demachi Futaba often has a queue.

title: Uji deeper: KyoAni, Euphonium, Medalist
titleJa: 宇治 深掘り（志を繋ぐ碑・ユーフォ聖地・木下アカデミー京都アイスアリーナ）
cost: Free; history park museum 800 JPY (optional)
summary: Beyond Uji Bridge and Daikichiyama (already in the list): Kumiko's bench on Ajirogi path, Agata Shrine, Asagiri Bridge and Keihan Uji Station from Sound! Euphonium. Visit the KyoAni 'monument that links hopes' in the Tea and Uji history park, and the Kyoto Ice Arena used for the Rengecha club in Medalist.
hook: Kumiko's river walk, and a quiet stop for the people of Kyoto Animation.
why: It adds a quiet moment for Kyoto Animation, whose shows they like, and more Uji scenes on the same half day.
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10. History park open 9:00–17:00, no regular closed day, park is free. The city asks visitors not to leave flowers or offerings at the monument. There is no fixed KyoAni Shop store

title: Haruhi: Nishinomiya's last winter
titleJa: 涼宮ハルヒの憂鬱 聖地巡礼 西宮（西宮北高校・甲陽園）
cost: Hankyu trains approx 400 JPY; cafe approx 700 JPY
summary: Nishinomiya is the town of Haruhi Suzumiya. See the Nishinomiya-Kitaguchi Station area (Endless Eight), take the Hankyu line to Koyoen, walk past Yuki Nagato's apartment area and climb the steep 'Haruhi hill' to Nishinomiya Kita High School, North High in the anime.
hook: Climb the Haruhi hill before North High changes its name in 2027.
why: The school closes as 'Nishinomiya Kita' at the end of March 2027, so this is the last winter to see the real North High.
winterNote: New route day 10, on the way to Itami Airport (20 min by bus/train). Official Haruhi site: the school merges and becomes Nishinomiya Kurakuen High School after March 2027. School is outside only (the

title: Mazda Museum day from Osaka
titleJa: マツダミュージアム（広島）
cost: Tour free; Shin-Osaka–Hiroshima Shinkansen approx 10,000–11,000 JPY each way
summary: A free guided tour at Mazda's home in Hiroshima: rotary engines, the RX-7 line, the 787B Le Mans winner, and a view of a real assembly line. From Osaka it is a day trip: Shinkansen to Hiroshima (about 1 h 25), then 5 min to Mukainada.
hook: See the rotary engine story and a real Mazda line, free.
why: Rotary RX-7s are JDM icons, and it is the only big car-maker tour open to walk-in tourists on this route; Hiroshima okonomiyaki is a bonus.
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10 (weekdays only; no weekend tours). One English tour a day (meet 14:15 at the head office lobby, shuttle bus). Book online, up to 3 months ahead (from late Oct 2026). Museum close

title: Toyota Hokkaido plant tour, Tomakomai
titleJa: トヨタ自動車北海道 工場見学（苫小牧）
cost: Free
summary: Toyota's Hokkaido factory in Tomakomai, about 30 min by car from New Chitose Airport, makes automatic and CVT gearboxes. The free 90-minute tour shows people and robots working side by side.
hook: The one Toyota factory you can still walk through on this trip.
why: The Toyota City plant tours are stopped, so this is the real Toyota factory they can see, and it is on the way from the airport.

why: It catches the Shirakawa-go light-up on Sun Jan 24, adds two anime towns (Hyouka, Your Name), a black castle in snow and Furano's dry powder.

hook: A whole hill set on fire in Nara, then a week of Hokkaido snow.
why: Pegasis gets 3 Niseko ski days and Aoki time to learn, the west part still has Kyoto, Uji and the one-night Nara fire festival.

title: JR pass check for west route
titleJa: JRパス比較（西ルート）
cost: Nationwide JR Pass 7 days: ¥50,000 until Sep 30, 2026, ¥53,000 from Oct 1, 2026 (+ special ticket for Nozomi, e.g. Tokyo–Shin-Osaka ¥4,960). JR-covered legs per version: A ~¥20,000 (Hikari Mishima→Nagoya ¥8,440, Nagoya→Kyoto ¥5,910, Kansai locals); B ~¥18,000 (Azusa ¥6,730, Kanazawa→Kyoto ¥7,720, locals; buses not JR); C ~¥18,000 (Nozomi Tokyo→Kyoto ¥14,170, locals). The Nationwide JR Pass is ¥53,000 for 7 days from Oct 1, 2026, but the JR legs on this route cost only about ¥18,000–20,000.
hook: Add up the tickets first: the big pass loses you ¥30,000.
why: It saves about ¥30,000 per person compared with a Nationwide pass that many blogs still recommend.
winterNote: New route days 5–10. JR-West's Kansai Area Pass (1–4 days) stops sales on Sep 30, 2026; the Kansai Mini Pass (¥3,000, 3 days, JR local/rapid only, no Shinkansen, no Haruka) stays. A JR Pass bought now

title: Skip suitcases: Tokyo to Kyoto
titleJa: 宅急便で荷物を先に送る（東京→京都）
cost: Yamato cash price Kanto→Kansai: 120 size ¥2,040, 140 size ¥2,630, 160 size ¥3,020 (¥100 less if you bring it to a shop). Kansai→Hokkaido: 140 ¥3,810, 160 ¥4,180. A checked bag on Peach/Jetstar costs about ¥2,500–4,000, JAL/ANA includes 20 kg.
summary: On the west route, send the big suitcases with Yamato from the Tokyo hotel straight to the Kyoto hotel, and travel with a daypack through Fuji, Numazu/Matsumoto, Takayama and Nagoya. At the end, carry them on the plane to Hokkaido (cheaper than sending).
hook: Five towns in five days with only a daypack.
why: Buses to Kawaguchiko, Takayama and Shirakawa-go have little luggage space, and they change hotels 5 times before Kyoto.
